chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a man from you drinks a single draught of water, and Allah obligates Paradise for him because of it.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, he takes a vessel, places it to his mouth, recites the Name (of Allah), then drinks. Then he moves it away while still desirous of it, praises Allah, then returns to drink. Then he moves it away, praises Allah, then returns to drink. Then he moves it away, praises Allah. Thus, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, obligates Paradise for him because of it.'

key_terms.يَشْتَهِيهِ: He desires it / is still craving it

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for drinking water with gratitude and self-restraint according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate how mundane acts like drinking water become acts of worship when performed with specific etiquette (adab) and mindfulness. The detailed description of pausing while still desirous and praising Allah emphasizes the Shia concept of transforming physical sustenance into spiritual elevation, thereby earning Paradise through consistent, conscious gratitude.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let the man from you drink the water, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Obligate the Paradise upon him due to it’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Let him take a container and place it upon his mouth, so he should Name (Bismillah), then he should drink. Then he should prevent it while he is desirous from it, so he should Praise Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, then return to drinking. Then he should prevent it, and he should Praise Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, then repeat the drinking. Then he should prevent it, and he should Praise Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>. Thus, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Obligate for him, due to it, the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Basir who has said the following: “
Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘One of you drinks water and for this Allah admits him into paradise.’

The Imam then said, ‘He picks up the bowl of water and places it in his mouth, then mentions the name of Allah and then he drinks. He then removes it from his mouth and expresses praise for Allah, even though he still has a desire to drink. He then drinks and removes the bowl of water from his mouth and expresses praise for Allah. He then drinks and then removes and expresses praise for Allah. Thus, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, deems his admission to paradise necessary.’”
